text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: contbatch path p99 latency spike detected in us-west-2. p99 jumped to 1.8s over last 5m (baseline ~220ms). autoscale healthy. tagging route: /v1/generate (streaming).
incident-bot: page created -> pagerduty:PD-INC-4721; severity: P1; notified: oncall@sre.team :rotating_light:
maria: I’m on it — pulling dashboards now. which customers hit this?
devin: seeing a cluster of streaming stalls correlated with large batch sizes on mixed-seqlen workloads. traces show long wait in contbatch scheduler for pack formation.
jia: can we confirm this is contbatch and not kv eviction / paging? I see a small uptick in KV misses but not enough to justify 1.8s p99.
ken: summary of metrics I pulled: contbatch_inflight ⬆️, avg_batch_size ⬆️ (from 12->28), pack_wait_ms median 200 -> 900, p99 queuing time ~1.1s. CPU/GPU utilization normal.
maria: good - sounds like scheduling/pack formation. any recent rollout to packing algorithm?
lucy: yes, we rolled scheduler tweak yesterday that increased max_pack_delay from 8ms -> 30ms to boost throughput for cold embeddings. maybe exposing mixedlen amplification.
devin: that matches. longer pack delay + mixed seq lengths -> big clients with short seqs stuck waiting for long seqs to fill batch. leads to tail amplification for streaming.
sre-ops: immediate mitigation options: 1) reduce max_pack_delay back to 8ms 2) enforce max_batch_size cap for streaming routes 3) route streaming requests to preemptive queue. which should we try first?
maria: reduce max_pack_delay -> quickest. can someone run the control-plane change? I can do fallback if sticky.
jenkins-bot: deploy job queued: change-config/contbatch/max_pack_delay -> 8ms (manifest: scheduler-v2)
devin: before full revert, let's try per-route cap. for /v1/generate+streaming set max_batch_size=12 and preemptive=true. that will keep short requests fast.
jia: agree, per-route change safer. but per-route change may take 30-45s to propagate; pack_delay revert is immediate-ish. do pack_delay then per-route cap.
ken: running command to change global pack delay now:
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/configs/scheduler -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"max_pack_delay_ms":8}'
```
ken: applied. scheduler config version bumped to v2.14.1.
maria: seeing pack_wait_ms drop on first host stream - p50/p95 down. p99 still elevated but trending.
sre-ops: pushing per-route cap to streaming route now:
```
PATCH /routes/streaming/v1/generate
{
  "max_batch_size": 12,
  "allow_preemptive": true
}
```
sre-ops: pushed, rolling out to us-west-2 router pool (10 hosts).
devin: monitoring tail — p99 down to 680ms after both changes. still higher than baseline but much improved.
jia: any customer-facing impact? which tenants saw increased latencies?
maria: query logs show 4 customers with >30% of requests impacted, most are internal test tenants and one small SaaS customer (acme-retail). I DM'd account team to prepare possible notice.
lucy: long-term: we need smarter pack gating for mixed seq lengths, maybe seq-length bucketing or max-wait-per-length. current single delay heuristic is too coarse.
ken: also consider KV prefix caching to avoid pack waits for clients that reuse prefixes.
sre-ops: reopened followup ticket: INF-7893 "contbatch: mixed-seqlen bucketing + per-route batching policies" assigned to devin & lucy. ETA triage meeting 14:00 PT.
maria: who wants the handoff if this ramps down? I can stay on for another 30m then hand to devin.
devin: I’ll take handoff at 14:20 PT. please add context to the incident timeline.
incident-bot: Incident INF-4721 created. severity=P1. timeline event: config revert (max_pack_delay->8ms) and per-route cap applied.
ken: small note: noticed one host still reporting sporadic 1.2s p99 — SSHing to capture logs. possible extra-long sequence (>>4k tokens) on a single connection causing KV cache thrash.
jia: if we find a large outlier client we should blackhole-longstreams temporarily or route to Dedicated capacity to avoid multi-tenant impact.
maria: action list posted: [1] Observe for 30m; [2] If p99 <500ms across region -> close; else escalate to oncall-sre for paging. [3] Customer comms: draft if acme-retail > 5% requests still impacted.
devin: also enabling streaming fallback to lighter model variant for 2% of requests as a safety net (rolling). command below to enable rollout 2%:
```
POST /rollouts
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "variant": "fp16-small", "percentage": 2 }
```
devin: rollout started. will abort if quality alerts fire.
lucy: leaving detailed notes in INF-7893 with profiler traces. we should avoid reintroducing high pack_delay without seq-bucketing.
maria: thanks team. I’m marking this as 'mitigated' but not resolved. taking the 30m watch and will update timeline. oncall-bot: closing automated page for now (status: mitigated) :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Pager duty note: PD-INC-4721 acknowledged by maria.
ken: appended logs from host-17 for trace (snip):
```
[2026-03-15T13:02:11Z] request id=abc123 seq_len=3 enqueued, waiting for pack fill
[2026-03-15T13:02:11Z] request id=abc124 seq_len=1200 enqueued, pack waiting
[2026-03-15T13:02:12Z] pack formed size=28 wait_ms=920 -> dispatch
[2026-03-15T13:02:12Z] stream connection id=conn55 stall 1100ms
```
maria: last check p99=420ms p95=200ms p50=95ms. moving to monitoring state. final notes: root cause = scheduler config (max_pack_delay increase) combined with mixed sequence lengths causing pack formation tail amplification. mitigations: revert pack_delay, per-route max_batch cap, fallback rollout. followups: INF-7893 (bucketing), log-based client detection, customer comms if needed.
devin: noted. I’ll own the follow-up and the 14:00 triage. handing off as discussed.
maria: handing off to devin now. thanks all :pray:
